questions.question: Which acid does vinegar contain?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acetic acid.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **Vinegar is a sour liquid** that is made by the fermentation of numerous dilute alcoholic liquids into a liquid **containing acetic acid.**
 
• Vinegar can be made from any liquid that is capable of being converted into alcohol in a two-step process. 
 
• Vinegar usually contains 5–8 per cent of ac**etic acid **by volume.
 
• Acetic acid is typically formed by the fermentation of ethanol or sugars by acetic acid bacteria.
 
• Vinegar is primarily used in the culinary arts: as a flavorful, acidic.
 
• The conversion of ethanol(CH3CH2OH) and oxygen(O2) to acetic acid(CH3COOH) are followed by the following reaction:
 
 
• CH3CH2OH + O2 → CH3COOH + H2O

questions.question: Select the synthetic indicator from among the given options.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Methyl orange**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Methyl orange** is a synthetic indicator used primarily in titrations due to its clear and distinct color change.
 
• It is used to determine the pH of a solution, changing color at a pH of approximately 3.1 to 4.4.
 
• In acidic solutions, methyl orange turns red, whereas in basic solutions, it turns yellow.
 
• This indicator is particularly useful for titrations involving weak bases and strong acids.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Litmus Solution**

 
 
• Litmus is a natural indicator derived from lichens.
 
• It is commonly used to test whether a solution is acidic or basic.
 
• Acidic solutions turn blue litmus paper red, while basic solutions turn red litmus paper blue.
 
 
 
• **Turmeric**
 
 
• Turmeric is a natural indicator that turns red in basic conditions.
 
• It remains yellow in acidic and neutral solutions.
 
• It is commonly used in household experiments to test for the presence of bases.
 
 
 
• **Cabbage Juice**
 
 
• Red cabbage juice is a natural pH indicator.
 
• It changes color over a wide pH range, from red in acidic conditions to green/yellow in neutral conditions, and blue/purple in basic conditions.
 
• It is often used in educational settings for pH experiments.
 
 
 
• **Indicators**
 
 
• An indicator is a substance that changes color to indicate the presence of an acid or base.
 
• They are widely used in titrations to determine the endpoint of a chemical reaction.
 
• Indicators can be synthetic (like methyl orange) or natural (like litmus, turmeric, and cabbage juice).

questions.question: Which acid is predominantly present in tomatoes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Oxalic acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oxalic acid** is a dicarboxylic acid that is found in many plants, including tomatoes.
 
• It is a strong acid and can be harmful if ingested in large quantities.
 
• With the molecular formula C₂H₂O₄, oxalic acid is a dicarboxylic acid. It is also referred to as oxiric acid or ethanedioic acid.
 
• There are numerous plants and vegetables that contain this chemical component.
 
• With the condensed formula HOOC-COOH, it is the most basic dicarboxylic acid and has a more acidic nature than acetic acid.
 
• Other acids mentioned in the options are also present in tomatoes, but in smaller amounts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acetic acid** is the main acid in vinegar and is also found in tomatoes, but in much lower concentrations than oxalic acid.
 
• **Carbonic acid **is formed when carbon dioxide dissolves in water and is not naturally present in tomatoes.
 
• **Tartaric acid **is found in grapes and is commonly used in winemaking.

questions.question: Which of the following is a natural indicator for acid and base?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**China rose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **China rose**, scientifically known as **Hibiscus rosa-sinensis**, is a natural indicator for acids and bases.
 
• It is widely used in experiments to determine the **pH** of substances.
 
• The petals of the flower exhibit a **color change** based on the pH of the solution it is exposed to:
 
• In an **acidic medium**, the color changes to **dark pink or magenta.**
 
• In a **basic medium**, the color changes to **greenish-yellow.**

 
• This property makes it a **natural and environmentally friendly indicator** in science experiments.
 
• China rose indicator is derived from the **petals of the flower** by boiling them in water.
 
• Such natural indicators are often preferred for their **non-toxic and biodegradable** nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Curry tree**__

 __
 
• **Curry tree**, scientifically known as **Murraya koenigii**, is a tropical to sub-tropical tree native to **India and Sri Lanka**.
 
• Its leaves are commonly used as a **spice in Indian cuisine** but have no known properties as a natural indicator.
 
• The tree is also valued for its **medicinal properties**, such as aiding digestion and treating infections.
 
 
 
• **Fungi**__
 __
 
• **Fungi** are a diverse group of **eukaryotic organisms** that include yeasts, molds, and mushrooms.
 
• They are primarily used in **fermentation, medicine production (e.g., antibiotics like penicillin)**, and decomposition.
 
• Fungi are not known to act as natural indicators for acids and bases.
 
 
 
• **Algae**__
 
 
• **Algae** are photosynthetic organisms found in **a variety of aquatic environments.**
 
• They are primarily valued for their role in **oxygen production** and as a source of **biofuels and food supplements** such as spirulina.
 
• Algae are not used as natural indicators in acid-base experiments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity Series:**

 
 
• The reactivity series is a list of metals arranged in order of their decreasing reactivity.
 
• Highly reactive metals like potassium and sodium are placed at the top, while less reactive ones like gold and platinum are at the bottom.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Reactivity:**
 
 
• Reactivity depends on the ability of an element to lose electrons and form positive ions.
 
• Metals that lose electrons easily, such as potassium, are more reactive.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Metals Based on Reactivity:**
 
 
• Highly reactive metals like potassium are used in chemical reactions and compounds but require careful handling.
 
• Less reactive metals like gold are used in jewelry and electronics due to their resistance to corrosion.
 
 
 
• **Storage of Reactive Metals:**
 
 
• Metals like potassium are stored in oil to prevent reactions with air and moisture.
 
• Magnesium and copper can be stored in open air but may oxidize over time.

questions.question: Which of the following naturally occurring acids is present in ant stings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Methanoic acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The acid present in an ant sting is Formic acid.
 
• Formic acid (systematically called methanoic acid) is the simplest carboxylic acid.
 
• Molecular formula: HCOOH
 
• It is quite fatal for those ants as after stinging, their stinger is lost after which formic acid is forcibly released from their poison gland.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Oxalic acid is an organic compound found in many plants. These include leafy greens, vegetables, fruits, cocoa, nuts, and seeds
 
• Lactic acid is a natural organic acid, found in milk and other food products such as meat and beer.
 
 
• It is used in the food industry as a preservative, flavor enhancer, and acid adjustment.
 
 
 
• Citric acid is found naturally in citrus fruits, like lemons and limes.
 
 
• It gives them their tart, sour taste.

questions.question: Which of the following household items contains sulphuric acid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Battery.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Battery acid **is **sulfuric acid **that has been diluted with water to attain a 37% concentration level.
 
• This particular type of acid is used in sealed lead-acid batteries.
 
• Batteries contain acid because it's fundamental to the electrochemical reaction that takes place.
 
• Also referred to as battery electrolyte, battery acid is the medium that carries the electrical flow between positive and negative electrodes.
 
• Batteries use a combination of lead plates and an electrolyte consisting of a diluted sulphuric acid to convert electrical energy into potential chemical energy and back again.
 
• Although this acid allows us to have portable power in the form of SLA batteries, the actual acid can be extremely dangerous. 
 
• It's corrosive nature literally melts any bodily tissue it comes in contact with. When it comes in contact with soil it will actually contaminate it for an extended period of time depending on the concentration of the acid. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vinegar:**

 
 
• Vinegar is a combination of acetic acid and water made by a two-step fermentation process.
 
• First, yeast feed on the sugar or starch of any liquid from a plant food such as fruits, whole grains, potatoes, or rice.
 
• This liquid ferments into alcohol.
 
• The alcohol is then exposed to oxygen and the acetic acid bacteria Acetobacter to ferment again over weeks or months, forming vinegar. 
 
• Vinegar contains five to eight per cent solution of acetic acid in water.
 
• Vinegar is an essential component of most pickling brines, where acetic acid also functions as a natural preservative.
 
• Vinegar is also used to stimulate chemical reactions that take place during cooking and baking.
